The test image shows a tomato leaf with yellowish/chlorotic patches on the upper surface, mostly green overall with no distinct dark lesions, powdery coating, or water-soaked areas. The pale patches are irregular and diffuse, suggesting Leaf Mold as the top candidate.

The reference Leaf Mold image shows a very similar pattern: green leaf with irregular yellow/pale patches on the upper surface, diffuse without distinct dark borders. This matches the test image well.

Key observations from test image:
- Single tomato leaflet, mostly green
- Yellow/chlorotic patches on upper surface, irregular distribution
- No dark lesions with concentric rings (rules out Early Blight)
- No powdery white coating (rules out Powdery Mildew)
- No small dark specks (rules out Bacterial Speck)
- No mosaic/mottled distortion (rules out CMV)
- No visible water-soaked lesions (rules out Late Blight)

The yellowing pattern on the upper leaf surface with the texture visible is consistent with Leaf Mold (*Fulvia fulva*), which causes yellow spots on the upper surface.
